newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW - UAE's Fal shifts focus to cargo trade.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - UAE's Fal shifts focus to cargo trade.

text.p: The Middle East's stagnant fuel oil bunker market has prompted privately-owned Fal Oil Co. Ltd to focus on cargo trade to supply the Indian sub-continent and east Africa, general manager Mohamad Osman said on Wednesday.
Osman told Reuters in an interview the Mideast bunker market, based in Fujairah in the United Arab Emirates (UAE), was sizable at one million tonnes a month (214,000 barrels-per-day).
But he said he did not see much growth in demand and thought it may even be decreasing due to a reduction in the number of turbine ships.
Fujairah is the third largest bunkering centre in the world after Singapore and Rotterdam.
"The fuel oil market is very small," Osman said. "That is the problem."

He said Fal, one of the earliest private companies to start bunker marketing in Fujairah, has since been joined by Mideast trader and refiner Metro, Avin, the marketing arm of Greek Motor Oil Hellas and U.S. major Texaco Inc. and medium distillates such as gasoline, diesel and jet-kerosene, Osman said.
But it was too early to settle any feedstock supply term contracts, he said.
Production will be targetted at both local consumption with the balance to the Indian-subcontinent and east Africa, he said.
Fal is already establishing its presence in the cargo market by regularly participating in spot tenders by India and Pakistan.

Competition has further heated up with Metro boosting its presence in the region at the begining of the year by commssioning its new 35,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) Fujairah refinery and starting to export fuel oil to the Far East.
Fal, based in Sharjah, plans to increase its cargo trading once it starts up a 42,000 bpd refinery in the first quarter of 1998, Osman said.

Fal's 100 percent-owned Sharjah Oil Refining Company Limited is 25 km out of Sharjah, near the Saudi condensate pipeline because it plans to blend the high quality oil with Gulf crude, such as light Omani crude, to use as a feedstock to produce mainly light

Osman said it currently buys supplies mainly from the state-owned Bahrain National Oil Company (Banoco) and Caltex Bahrain, the joint-venture between U.S. majors Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp joint-venture.
"The volumes are big," Osman said, but decline to reveal the exact amount. "But these are old ties...we have been more than 12 years with Bahrain."
